targets.note: one decade per swept axis. The question is whether the crossover appears and moves as v0 and D_R move, not what its coefficient is to two figures. explore's tie band applies: anything inside 10x is a tie

constraint_notes: REVISION 4 CHANGES ONE UNIT AND NOTHING ELSE. n_particles moves from `count` to `1`. The reason is that the budget gate compares a wall clock and a storage estimate against ceilings, both are the particle count times a step or frame count, and a count declared with an amount dimension makes that product unspellable -- particles-times-steps over a rate is amount-seconds and no unit in the registry is that. The estimate could not be written, so no active plan could pass the gate. Every value and every other unit is revision 3's.

the person's question of 2026-09-23, verbatim in intent: simulate active Brownian particles and investigate how translational dynamics depend on v0, D_R and D_T; vary v0 and D_R over appropriate ranges; determine how the MSD, persistence time, persistence length and effective translational diffusivity change; examine short- and long-time regimes and identify the crossover from persistent or ballistic motion to long-time diffusive motion; quantify the scaling from log-log MSD slopes; examine D_eff(t) and its log-log slope; determine how the crossover time and length depend on v0, D_R and D_T; collapse with dimensionless quantities such as the Peclet number

THE PROPULSION IS A FIXED SPEED, ruled by the person on 2026-09-23. For these free particles it changes the declaration and not the trajectory: a fixed force F along the orientation gives velocity F/gamma of fixed magnitude, so the two models coincide where there is nothing to push against. It will matter to the interacting questions

THE SWEEP VALUES ARE THIS SEAT'S, delegated by the person on 2026-09-23 with the words pick reasonable values and run. They are therefore `assumed:` at E5 with falsifiers, not E6: a delegated choice recorded with its reason and what would overturn it is what `assumed:` is for, and E6 is a value presented as evidence it is not. What is NOT this seat's is the physical anchor -- d, T and eta are the store's, at E2 and E3, so D_T is the actual laboratory system's and not an invention

the anchor is the laboratory's own tracer: 5 um in water at 293 K gives D_T = 0.09 um^2/s by Stokes-Einstein, and the sphere's Stokes-Einstein-Debye rotational diffusivity 3*D_T/d^2 = 0.01 rad^2/s is the CENTRE of the D_R sweep. The sweep then deliberately breaks that tie, because the person asked for D_R and D_T to be varied independently and a sphere in a bulk fluid cannot do that. Off-centre points are a model with no single particle diameter behind them, which is legitimate here -- abp_free declares no diameter -- and is exactly why peclet_number_steric is not this question's collapse variable

REVISION 3 IS ONE OPERATING POINT, NOT THE NINE-POINT GRID OF REVISION 2. Revision 2 tried to put a sweep on one card and produced numbers from two different corners -- the fast end for D_R and the slow end for the persistence time -- which A1 caught as a check 17 mismatch. The module was right and the card was wrong. A sweep has NO single tightest corner: A1 wants the fastest point and A2 the slowest, so no one point satisfies every axis. `varies_with` landed in common.schema.json for exactly this and is the way back to the sweep, but the field is filled by axes_abp, which is another seat's. This revision therefore runs the single most informative point and the sweep follows.

the point is the Stokes-Einstein-Debye centre at Pe_thermal = 100, so every number describes one real 5 um particle in water at 293 K driven at 3 um/s. Lambda = 1e4 puts tau_1 = 0.01 s and tau_R = 100 s four decades apart, and the save interval of 1e-3 s puts the shortest lag a decade below tau_1 -- so ALL THREE REGIMES are inside one window: thermal at slope 1, ballistic approaching 1.98, and effective diffusion at slope 1

bead_diameter is carried because the axis modules read it, and it is NOT a parameter of abp_free. The configuration declares no pair interaction, no wall, no obstacle and no diameter. It appears here only as the provenance of D_T and of the sweep's centre, and any axis bound that compares a length to it is bounding something this model does not have

peclet_max is carried in the STERIC convention, v0/(d*D_R), because that is the convention axes_abp's formulas assume. It is NOT this question's collapse variable and must not be read as one: peclet_thermal_max is. The two are not proportional across this grid -- that is the whole point of sweeping D_R away from Stokes-Einstein-Debye -- and peclet_number_steric's own registry entry says it is defined only where an interaction length exists

A3 abstains and the abstention is the physics: nothing couples a free particle to its periodic image, so with unwrapped coordinates the MSD is independent of the box. A7 abstains too -- self-propulsion is the model and not a driving protocol applied to it

the record length is 20 persistence times at the SLOWEST point, which is the longest run the grid asks for, and the save interval is a thousandth of the persistence time at each point. That resolves the thermal regime below tau_1 = D_T/v0^2 at Lambda of 1 and 100 and NOT at Lambda of 1e4, where the first lag already sits ten times above tau_1. Said in advance rather than discovered: at the top of the sweep the earliest of the three regimes is outside the window on purpose, because resolving it there would cost a factor of ten in storage to see a sliver
no experimental counterpart is measured and nothing here is fitted to data

numbers.name: bead_diameter
numbers.note: the laboratory's tracer, measured by the operator on 2026-09-19. Provenance of D_T and of the sweep's centre, NOT a parameter of abp_free

numbers.name: temperature
numbers.note: the room's, read off a thermometer. In this configuration temperature is constitutive -- a parameter of the noise amplitude with no mechanism that could fail to realise it -- so citing it records why the value was chosen and is not evidence about the model

numbers.name: viscosity
numbers.note: pure water; the entry's validity runs 288 to 298 K and the temperature above is inside it

numbers.name: translational_diffusivity
numbers.note: held fixed across the whole grid. One significant figure because the worst input carries one

numbers.name: rotational_diffusivity
numbers.note: the sphere's own Stokes-Einstein-Debye value, 3*D_T/d^2. This revision sits ON the realisable centre rather than off it, so every number here describes one physical particle. Unit 1/s and not rad^2/s: the registry gives rad the dimension A, so rad^2/s cannot enter any formula check 17 can evaluate, and a radian is dimensionless

numbers.name: persistence_time_expected
numbers.note: 1/((d-1)*D_R) is 1/D_R in two dimensions. Consistent with the rotational diffusivity above BY CONSTRUCTION, which revision 2 was not: it carried the sweep top for one and the sweep bottom for the other, and A1 failed check 17 on the mismatch

numbers.name: peclet_thermal
numbers.note: the collapse variable v0/sqrt((d-1)*D_R*D_T) at this operating point. 100 gives Lambda = 1e4, where the maximum log-log slope is 1.98 -- the ballistic regime is present and clean. At Pe_thermal of 10 the maximum is 1.79 and at 1 it is 1.12

numbers.name: peclet_max
numbers.note: THE STERIC CONVENTION v0/(d*D_R), 57.7 at this point, carried only because axes_abp's formulas read that name. Not the collapse variable

numbers.name: thermal_crossover_time
numbers.note: tau_1 = D_T/v0^2, the EARLY crossover where the thermal regime gives way to the ballistic one. The three-regime structure is the reason this number exists: the MSD starts at slope 1, not 2

numbers.name: persistence_length_expected
numbers.note: 289 um at one figure. It bounds nothing -- A3 abstains because a free particle is not coupled to its image -- and is recorded so that is visible

numbers.name: n_particles
numbers.note: non-interacting walkers, a statistics knob and not a density. A hundred keeps the trajectory inside two gigabytes at the save interval this point needs Unit 1 and not count, changed at revision 4. `count` carries an amount dimension in the registry and `1` does not, so a particle count declared as `count` cannot be multiplied into anything: particles times steps is an amount, and dividing that by a rate gives amount-seconds, which no unit spells. The cost estimates the envelope gate compares against ceilings are exactly that product, so they could not be written at all. This tree already follows the convention -- the interacting active question declares its per-arm particle counts dimensionless for the same reason, and an older goal carried a cube root of a count as `1` noting that the cube root of a count is not a count. Nothing physical changes; a hundred particles is a hundred particles.

numbers.name: record_length_persistence_times
numbers.note: ten persistence times, so the long-time plateau is entered and D_eff is read above the crossover rather than through it. Ten rather than twenty because the save interval this point needs makes every frame expensive

numbers.name: save_intervals_per_persistence_time
numbers.note: the save interval is tau_R/1e5 = 1e-3 s, which puts the shortest resolved lag a full decade BELOW tau_1 = 0.01 s. That is what buys the thermal regime, and it is the reason this point is expensive: 1e6 frames

assumptions.statement: The thermal Peclet number is set to 100 at this single operating point, where Lambda = 1e4 and the maximum log-log slope is 1.98. Chosen so the ballistic regime is present rather than marginal: at Pe_thermal of 10 the maximum slope is 1.79 and at 1 it is 1.12.
assumptions.falsifier: a run whose maximum log-log slope falls below 1.9, which would mean this point does not reach the regime it was chosen to reach

assumptions.statement: A thousand non-interacting walkers per point. Nothing physical picks this; it is the statistics knob, and the particles do not interact so it is not a density.
assumptions.falsifier: a statistical error on D_eff that this ensemble cannot reach inside budget

assumptions.statement: Twenty persistence times per run, so the long-time plateau is entered rather than approached and D_eff is read above the crossover.
assumptions.falsifier: a D_eff still drifting at the end of the record

assumptions.statement: A hundred thousand save intervals per persistence time, so the shortest lag sits a decade below tau_1 and all three regimes are inside the window. Chosen against the physics rather than against storage, and it costs about 1.6 GB against a 10 GB ceiling.
assumptions.falsifier: a log-log slope at the shortest lags that has not flattened, meaning the grid starts inside a regime it cannot resolve

kb_refs.claim: The particles in the bottle in use have a diameter of 5 micrometres, with a coefficient of variation no greater than 2 per cent, measured directly by the operator on 2026-09-19.
The laboratory's ambient temperature is 20 degrees Celsius, read off a thermometer by the operator. It is a reading and not a setpoint, and it is the room's rather than the sample's.
Dynamic viscosity of pure water near 293 K is of order one millipascal second, and it changes by roughly two percent per kelvin in that neighbourhood.
